t: This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This is a bare effective-date clause that only states when the Act takes effect. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government plays any role. There is no tempting participation reading here beyond the generic word "Act."
fable.s: This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This section only says when the Act takes effect. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Because nothing in the text even touches on participation, the label is No and the quoted span is empty.
opus.b: This is an effective-date clause. The only thing that might tempt a "Yes" is that it reads like formal statutory language, but no outside party has any role in a federal decision, so it doesn't meet the definition.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely specifies the effective date of the statute. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "enactment" implies a legislative process involving public input, but the section itself only states the effective date of the law. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or participation. The text is purely procedural regarding the timing of the statute's application.
